# ReqFlow — product definition

> Working name. One page, the source of truth for **what** we build. **How** is in
> [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), **who builds what** in [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).

## Problem

Defining the next generation of a BMW vehicle means working out what customers will value 3–5 years
from now. Today product managers do this by hand: they read customer feedback, BMW equipment and
sales data, customer studies and competitor and market information, then turn it into requirements.
It is slow, inconsistent and hard to trace. Months later nobody can say why a requirement exists,
what evidence backs it, or who decided it.

## Product in one sentence

A visual, n8n-style **workflow** turns raw customer and market data into **evidence-linked, prioritized
car requirements**. A product manager then reviews, challenges and decides on them on a separate
**Requirements** page, and every step is recorded in an **audit trail**.

> Customer requirement = customer-relevant attribute of a car. (BMW briefing)

## Users

- **Product Manager (primary).** Owns the requirement set for one vehicle line × market. Makes every decision.
- **Analyst / PM ops (secondary).** Builds and tunes workflows, connects data and adjusts scoring in Settings.

## The app — three pages (plus the audit trail)

| Page | What the user does |
|---|---|
| **Workflow** | Drag nodes onto a canvas and connect them (BMW datasets, web research, AI analysis steps, scoring, a PM-review gate, publish), then run the workflow. Each node shows its status, item counts and logs, and you can click a node to see the data it produced. A run **pauses at the review gate**. |
| **Requirements** (output) | Shows the result: what the next car should offer. Each requirement has an ID, title, description, measurable targets, category, score breakdown, priority with rationale, evidence level, assumptions, uncertainties, conflicting evidence and status. A detail view goes from requirement → findings → verbatim evidence → source. The PM can **approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge** each one, and must give a rationale every time. |
| **Settings** | Choose the AI provider and models, the web research provider and allowed domains, the prioritization weights and thresholds, the default scope (vehicle line, derivative, market, horizon) and the reviewer identity. |
| **Audit trail** | A chronological, append-only log: who or what (AI model, PM, system) changed what, when, from what to what, and why. Filterable down to one requirement. |

## Pipeline (default workflow template)

The pipeline mirrors the BMW process slide (`context/` image). The robot icon means the AI does the step on its own; the person icon means a human is involved.

```
Situation analysis      Structure & context            Requirements definition      Prioritization      Review         Documentation
──────────────────      ───────────────────            ───────────────────────      ──────────────      ──────         ─────────────
BMW feedback   ┐
Customer study ┤
Equipment data ┼─▶ extract signals ─▶ scope filter ─▶ cluster ─▶ derive ─▶ specify targets ─▶ score ─▶ 🧑 PM gate ─▶ publish / export
Sales volumes  ┤     (findings +       (drop regulatory, (themes,     (drafts)   (metrics,          (weighted,   (pause until   (Requirements
Web research   ┘      evidence)         engineering,      dedupe)                evidence level,    explainable)  PM decided)    page, JSON/CSV/MD)
                                         pricing)                                assumptions)
```

**Where AI acts on its own:** ingestion, signal extraction, scope filtering, clustering, drafting
requirements, specifying targets, scoring.
**Where a human must act:** approving, rejecting, deferring or editing a requirement, overriding a
priority, answering a challenge, and resuming the run after the gate. The AI can **never** set a
requirement to `approved` or `rejected`.

## Core objects (full schemas in `packages/core`)

- **Source** — a dataset, document or web page, with a reliability rating.
- **SourceRecord** — one comment, row or paragraph from a source.
- **Finding** — a normalized signal (`complaint`, `unmet_need`, `praise`, `competitor_advantage`,
  `market_trend` or `usage_pattern`). It always cites ≥ 1 verbatim evidence excerpt.
- **Theme** — a cluster of duplicate or related findings.
- **Requirement** — `REQ-<vehicle>-<market>-<nnn>`. Holds the description, targets, linked findings and
  sources, score, priority with rationale, **evidence level A–D**, assumptions, uncertainties,
  conflicting findings and **status** (`proposed → in_review → approved | rejected | deferred`, plus
  `challenged`).
- **AuditEvent** — actor, action, entity, before/after changes, rationale and timestamp. Never edited or deleted.

## Prioritization logic (explainable by design)

Six factors, each scored 0–5 with a one-line justification. On every factor, higher means "more worth doing":
customer impact · evidence strength · competitive gap · trend momentum (3–5 yr) · brand fit ·
ease (the inverse of rough effort/cost).

`score = 100 × Σ(weight × value) / (5 × Σ weight)`. The score maps to **must / should / could / won't**
using the thresholds set in Settings. The PM can override the priority, and the override is audited.
Evidence level is shown **next to** the score, never hidden inside it. A high score built on
D-level (assumption) evidence should catch the eye.

## Evidence levels

**A** — several independent sources including quantitative BMW data · **B** — several sources, mostly
qualitative · **C** — a single source or anecdotal · **D** — rests mainly on forward-looking assumptions.

## Scope rules (from the briefing)

- **In scope:** customer-facing attributes such as features, equipment, comfort, space, usability,
  infotainment and digital services, design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging
  *as the customer experiences them*, and variants and packages.
- **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, technical and engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases. The scope filter removes these, and every exclusion is logged with a reason.

## Demo scenario

**BMW 5 Series Sedan · EU · 5-year horizon.** This is our default. Confirm it once BMW's datasets arrive.
1. Open the default template, attach the BMW files, enable web research, and run.
2. Watch the nodes fill up, then click *extract signals* to see findings with their evidence.
3. The run pauses at the PM gate. On Requirements, open a must-have and trace it down to a verbatim customer quote.
4. Challenge one requirement. The AI answers. Edit one, approve one with a priority override, and reject one.
5. Resume the run, which publishes and exports. The audit trail shows the full history of one requirement.
6. Switch the scope to another series or market in Settings to show the workflow isn't a one-off.

## Deliverables checklist (briefing → where we show it)

- [ ] Concept and working prototype → the app and this document
- [ ] Structured sample list of requirements with all the required fields → Requirements page and export
- [ ] End-to-end workflow showing which steps the AI does alone and where a human must act → Workflow page and the diagram above
- [ ] Audit trail from source to decision → Audit trail page and the requirement History tab

## Non-goals for the hackathon

Authentication and roles (one demo reviewer identity), multi-user live collaboration, production
deployment and real-time streaming. Any of these can be mocked if the demo needs them.

# AGENTS.md — read this first

## What we're building

**ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge *"AI for Product Decision Making"*. An
n8n-style **workflow** turns customer and market data into prioritized, evidence-linked car
requirements. A PM reviews them on a **Requirements** page, and a **Settings** page configures the
app. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).

## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
  for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
  every decision.
- **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
  market** (ours: 5 Series Sedan, EU), but don't build a one-off.
- **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
  We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
- **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
  competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
  priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
  a decision status.
- **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
  design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
  and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
- **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
  handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
  beats shallow coverage of everything.
- **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
  requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
  business) → documentation and tracking. *"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."*

## Rules for every agent

1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
   something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
   contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
3. **No real data in git.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Use synthetic fixtures from
   `@reqflow/core/fixtures` until the real data arrives. Never commit or print API keys.
4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
   sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
   requirement writes an AuditEvent.
6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
   `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also load the page and check it.

## Commands (repo root, Node ≥ 22.13)

```
npm install          # once
npm run dev          # web app on http://localhost:3000
npm test             # vitest, all packages
npm run typecheck    # all workspaces
npm run format       # prettier
```

# Architecture

## Stack

| Concern | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Language | TypeScript everywhere (npm workspaces) | One shared contract for UI, engine and nodes |
| Web app | Next.js 16 (App Router) + React 19 + Tailwind 4 | Pages and API route handlers in one app |
| Workflow canvas | `@xyflow/react` (React Flow) | The standard n8n-style node editor |
| Schemas | Zod 4 | Runtime validation and TS types from a single source; `z.toJSONSchema` drives the config forms |
| LLM | Claude API (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`) behind `LlmClient`, plus a `mock` provider | Swappable; works offline and in tests |
| Persistence | SQLite via built-in `node:sqlite` (`data/app.db`) | Zero setup, no native build |
| Tests | Vitest (root config, colocated `*.test.ts`) | Fast, TS-native |

## Repo layout

```
.
├── AGENTS.md  PRODUCT.md  README.md   ← start here
├── context/                           ← original hackathon briefing (read-only)
├── docs/                              ← ARCHITECTURE, WORKSTREAMS, decisions/ (ADRs)
├── data/
│   ├── raw/        (gitignored)       ← BMW-provided datasets
│   ├── uploads/    (gitignored)       ← files uploaded through the UI
│   └── samples/                       ← small synthetic datasets for dev
├── packages/
│   ├── core/       ← CONTRACT: domain schemas, service interfaces, API shapes, fixtures
│   ├── engine/     ← node contract + registry (done); graph validation + executor (WS1)
│   ├── nodes/      ← node implementations, one folder per workstream + default template
│   ├── llm/        ← LlmClient implementations: anthropic, mock (WS7)
│   └── db/         ← SQLite repositories, AuditLogger, FileStore (WS1)
└── apps/web/       ← Next.js: pages, components/<area>/, app/api/ route handlers, server/ wiring
```

Dependency direction (no cycles): `core ← engine ← nodes`, `core ← llm`, `core ← db`, and
`apps/web` → all of them. Only `apps/web/src/server` (server-only) wires concrete services together.

## Data flow: one envelope on every edge

Each node has **one input and one output**. The input and output are a `PipelineData`
(`sources, records, findings, themes, requirements`). A node reads the keys it `consumes` and returns
the envelope with the keys it `produces` updated. When a node has several incoming edges, the engine
combines them with `mergePipelineData` (concatenate, de-duplicate by `id`, later edge wins).

```ts
defineNode({
  type: "analysis.extract_signals", category: "analysis",
  consumes: ["records"], produces: ["findings"],
  configSchema: z.object({ batchSize: z.number().int().default(25) }),
  async run(input, config, ctx) { /* ctx.llm, ctx.audit, ctx.log … */ return { status: "ok", data: { ...input, findings } }; },
});
```

## Engine semantics (WS1 implements, everyone relies on)

1. **Validate before running.** Every node type is registered, the graph is acyclic, edges point at existing
   nodes, and each node's `config` parses with its `configSchema`. If anything fails, the run fails before it starts,
   with per-node errors.
2. **Execute in topological order.** The input to a node is the merge of its parents' outputs (a source node gets
   an empty envelope). Store each node's output (for "click node → inspect data") and update
   `NodeRun` status, counts, logs and progress.
3. **Failure.** A node that throws is marked `failed` with the error message. Its downstream nodes are marked `skipped`
   and the run is marked `failed`. No partial publish happens.
4. **Pause / resume.** A `review.*` node returns `{status:"paused"}`. The run becomes `waiting_for_review`.
   `POST /api/runs/:id/resume` reloads the latest requirement versions from the DB (the PM may have
   edited them), re-invokes the gate with `ctx.resumed = true`, and continues.
5. **Cancel.** The run's `AbortSignal` fires. Nodes must stop promptly.
6. **Audit.** The engine logs `run.*` events. Nodes log what they create or change. The API logs human actions.

## HTTP API (`apps/web/src/app/api`, JSON, errors use the `ApiError` shape)

| Method & path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/nodes` | Node catalog: `NodeCatalogEntry[]` (palette and config JSON Schema) |
| `GET/POST /api/workflows` · `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/workflows/:id` | Workflow CRUD (`Workflow`). PUT bumps `version` |
| `GET /api/templates` | Workflow templates (`BMW_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE`) |
| `POST /api/uploads` (multipart) | Store a BMW file → `{ fileId }` |
| `POST /api/workflows/:id/runs` | Start a run → `WorkflowRun` |
| `GET /api/runs/:id` | Run status (the UI polls about every 1 s while running) |
| `GET /api/runs/:id/nodes/:nodeId/output` | That node's output `PipelineData` |
| `POST /api/runs/:id/resume` · `POST /api/runs/:id/cancel` | Gate resume / cancel |
| `GET /api/requirements?runId&status&category&priority` | List (latest versions) |
| `GET /api/requirements/:id` | Requirement + expanded findings, evidence and sources + version list |
| `PATCH /api/requirements/:id` | `RequirementEdit` (rationale required) → new version and audit |
| `POST /api/requirements/:id/decision` | `RequirementDecision`. `challenge` makes the AI answer (`requirement.challenge_answered`) and sets the requirement back to `in_review` |
| `GET /api/audit?entityId&entityType&actorType&action&runId` | Audit events, ascending by time |
| `GET/PUT /api/settings` | `Settings` (PUT logs `settings.changed` with a diff) · `GET /api/settings/status` → which API keys are configured (booleans only) |
| `GET /api/export?runId&format=json\|csv\|md` | Requirement list export (logs `export.created`) |

## AI usage rules

- Use `ctx.llm.generateObject` with a Zod schema for every AI step. Invalid output → throw.
- **Never trust model-cited evidence.** The model returns `recordId` and `excerpt`. Code checks that the excerpt is
  a verbatim substring of that record, and drops or flags the finding if it isn't.
- Batch the records. Use `tier: "fast"` for per-record extraction and `default` for clustering, derivation and challenges.
- AI actors in the audit trail record the exact model id returned by the client.
- The `mock` provider must return schema-valid, deterministic output so the whole pipeline runs offline.
- Prompts live next to the node that uses them (`nodes/src/<area>/<node>.prompt.ts`).

## Persistence notes (WS1)

- Requirements are versioned: one row per `(id, version)`. "Current" means the max version.
- `audit_events` is insert-only, with no update or delete code path.
- Node outputs are stored per `(runId, nodeId)` as JSON.
- Resolve `DATABASE_PATH` and `UPLOAD_DIR` against the repo root (Next runs with `cwd = apps/web`).

# Workstreams — how to split the work across agents

Each workstream (WS) owns a set of paths, so parallel agents never edit the same files. Everything
builds against the contract in `packages/core` and the node contract in `packages/engine/src/node.ts`.
UI workstreams use `@reqflow/core/fixtures` until the API is live. Node workstreams test with
fixtures and the `mock` LLM.

## Kickoff prompt (paste into each agent, fill in the WS)

> You are agent **WS\<n\> (\<name\>)** on the ReqFlow repo. Read `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md`,
> `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and your section of `docs/WORKSTREAMS.md`. Build your workstream end to end,
> editing only your owned paths. Finish with: what you built, how you verified it (commands and
> results), any contract-change requests, and what is still open.

## Git

Use one branch per workstream (`ws1-engine`, `ws2-editor`, …), ideally in its own `git worktree`. Make small
commits and rebase on `main` often. To add a dependency, add it to **your own** package's
`package.json` only. If `package-lock.json` conflicts, run `npm install` again.

## Phases

0. **Done (lead):** repo skeleton, the contract (`core`), the node contract and registry, the default template, fixtures, and the app shell.
1. **Parallel:** WS1–WS8 below.
2. **Integration (lead):** wire services and the registry in `apps/web/src/server`, run the default template end
   to end with `mock`, then with Claude and the real BMW data, then polish the demo.

---

### WS0 — Lead / integrator (main session)
**Owns:** `packages/core/**`, `docs/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, root config files.
**Does:** merges branches, reviews and applies contract changes, runs integration (phase 2) and keeps docs current.

### WS1 — Engine, persistence & API
**Owns:** `packages/engine/**`, `packages/db/**`, `apps/web/src/app/api/**`, `apps/web/src/server/**`,
`apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts`, `packages/nodes/src/review/**`, `packages/nodes/src/output/**`.
**Builds:**
- **First,** a typed `lib/api-client.ts` covering every endpoint in ARCHITECTURE.md, so UI agents can code against it.
- Graph validation and the executor (topological run, merge, per-node output storage, failure → skipped, pause/resume, cancel).
- SQLite repositories, versioned requirements, append-only `AuditLogger`, `FileStore`, settings storage.
- All route handlers, with Zod validation on input and `ApiError` on failure. `server/` wires registry, LLM, web search and DB.
- Nodes: `review.pm_gate`, `output.publish`, `output.export` (JSON / CSV / Markdown).

**Done when:** executor tests pass with fake nodes (success, failure, multi-input merge, pause → resume,
cancel). Every endpoint works against SQLite. A run of fake nodes shows up in `GET /api/runs/:id`.

### WS2 — Workflow editor UI
**Owns:** `apps/web/src/app/workflow/**`, `apps/web/src/components/workflow/**`.
**Builds:** a React Flow canvas. The node palette comes from `GET /api/nodes`, grouped by category with
consumes/produces hints. A config side panel is rendered from `configJsonSchema`, including file upload for
`source.bmw_dataset`. Save and load workflows, and start a new one from a template. Add a run button with
live status, counts and logs on each node. Clicking a node opens an output inspector. A "waiting for PM
review" banner links to `/requirements`. Warn when a node consumes a key that nothing upstream produces.
**Done when:** you can build the default template by hand, save it, reload it, and see run states on the canvas (mocked until WS1 lands).

### WS3 — Requirements review & audit UI
**Owns:** `apps/web/src/app/requirements/**`, `apps/web/src/app/audit/**`,
`apps/web/src/components/requirements/**`, `apps/web/src/components/audit/**`.
**Builds:** a requirements list or board with filters and sorting. A detail page shows targets, a score
breakdown (factor × weight with notes), priority and rationale, an evidence level badge, assumptions,
uncertainties and conflicting evidence, and a drill-down from findings to verbatim excerpts to sources.
Add a decision bar (approve / reject / defer / challenge) where rationale is required, inline editing with
rationale, a History tab, a global audit timeline with before → after diffs and filters, a resume-run
action, and export.
**Done when:** every field from the briefing's deliverable list is visible for the fixture requirements,
and the decision and edit flows call the API client.

### WS4 — Settings & app shell
**Owns:** `apps/web/src/app/settings/**`, `apps/web/src/components/settings/**`,
`apps/web/src/components/shell/**`, `apps/web/src/components/ui/**` (shared primitives),
`apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/globals.css`.
**Builds:** a Settings form for every `Settings` field: LLM provider and models, API-key status (never the
key itself), research provider and domains, weight sliders with a live example score built on
`weightedTotal`, thresholds, default scope, and reviewer. It validates with the `Settings` schema. Also own the
visual system (tokens and shared UI primitives others reuse) and the app shell.
**Done when:** settings load, validate, save and appear as a `settings.changed` audit event, and the shell looks demo-ready.

### WS5 — BMW data ingestion
**Owns:** `packages/nodes/src/ingest/**`, `data/samples/**`.
**Builds:** the `source.bmw_dataset` node. Config: `fileId`, `datasetKind`, optional column mapping. It parses
the provided formats (CSV, XLSX and whatever BMW ships: check `data/raw/` once it arrives) into `Source` +
`SourceRecord[]` with locators and language. Structured datasets (equipment take rates, sales volumes)
also emit deterministic `usage_pattern` findings (for example a high take rate signals a basic expectation)
with evidence. Also write synthetic sample files in `data/samples/` that match the real formats.
**Done when:** each sample dataset ingests in tests, errors name the bad row or column, and no data is dropped silently.

### WS6 — Web research
**Owns:** `packages/nodes/src/research/**`.
**Builds:** the `source.web_research` node. It turns the scope into queries (competitors in the segment,
owner and press reviews, market and technology trends for the horizon), runs them through `ctx.web`, fetches
pages and extracts clean text into `SourceRecord`s, and sets the `Source` kind, publisher, date and
**reliability** (with the rule documented). It respects allowed and blocked domains and de-duplicates by URL.
Also implement `WebSearch` providers (`anthropic_web_search`, `tavily`) as factories that take keys as
arguments (WS1 wires them).
**Done when:** a recorded or offline test run produces sources with working URLs and reliability, and failures are logged rather than swallowed.

### WS7 — AI analysis & requirement derivation
**Owns:** `packages/llm/**`, `packages/nodes/src/analysis/**`, `packages/nodes/src/requirements/**`.
**Builds:** an `LlmClient` with a Claude provider and a deterministic `mock` provider (use the `claude-api`
skill for SDK details). The nodes are `analysis.extract_signals` (with verbatim-excerpt verification),
`analysis.scope_filter` (out-of-scope items logged with a reason), `analysis.cluster_themes`,
`requirements.derive` (customer-facing, actionable, IDs from `formatRequirementId`) and
`requirements.specify_targets` (measurable targets, evidence level per the A–D rule, Kano class,
assumptions, uncertainties, conflicting findings). Also export `answerChallenge(...)` for the API's
challenge flow.
**Done when:** fixture records → findings → themes → requirements runs fully offline with `mock`, all
outputs parse against the core schemas, and every finding's excerpt is verified.

### WS8 — Prioritization
**Owns:** `packages/nodes/src/prioritization/**`.
**Builds:** the `prioritization.score` node. Factors are computed deterministically where possible: customer
impact from mentions, sentiment and sales volume; evidence strength from independent sources × reliability
and evidence level; competitive gap from `competitor_advantage` findings; trend momentum from `market_trend`
findings. The LLM is used only where a judgement is needed (brand fit, ease), always with a one-line note.
It uses `weightedTotal` and `priorityForScore` and writes a readable `priorityRationale` naming the top drivers.
It also flags "high score, weak evidence".
**Done when:** scores are reproducible for the fixtures, changing Settings weights changes the ranking as
expected (tested), and each factor has a note a PM can understand.

I've set up the repo and written the product spec. Agents can now work in parallel without editing the same files. Typecheck, all 13 tests, the format check and the production build pass, and I opened the app in the browser to confirm the sidebar and all pages load.

**What's in it**
- **[PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md)** is the core product: the problem, the n8n-style Workflow page, the Requirements page where the PM decides, Settings, and an Audit trail. It also covers the pipeline, the prioritization formula, the A–D evidence levels, the scope rules and a demo script.
- **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** is the short brief for agents. It condenses the PDF, the RTF and the process slide, and adds 7 rules for every agent.
- **[docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md)** splits the work into 8 workstreams. Each one owns specific folders and has a "done when" check. It includes a kickoff prompt you paste into each agent with its workstream number.
- **[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)** covers the stack, folder layout, how data moves between workflow steps, how runs pause and resume for PM review, and the list of API endpoints.
- **`packages/core`** holds the shared data definitions every agent builds against: requirement, finding, source, audit event, workflow, settings. It also has synthetic 5 Series sample data, so the UI agents can start before the backend exists.

**Choices I made that you may want to change**
- **Stack:** TypeScript only, with Next.js 16, React Flow for the canvas, SQLite for storage, and Claude behind an interface. The default AI provider is an offline "mock", so agents don't spend API credits while building.
- **Demo scope:** 5 Series Sedan in the EU. Confirm this once BMW's data arrives.
- **Name:** "ReqFlow" is just a working name.
- **Extra page:** I added the Audit trail as a fourth page, because the briefing lists it as a deliverable.

**What's not built yet**
- No product features exist yet. Every page is a placeholder that names the workstream that owns it.
- The workflow engine, database, AI client and all 11 workflow steps are empty slots for the agents.

**About the delegated work:** agy wrote the sample data after falling back from Opus to Gemini because the Opus quota was used up. Its tests passed, but some of the data broke our own rules. One requirement was justified by regulation, one read like an engineering spec, and the audit history contradicted itself. I fixed those and made the tests stricter. ## 1) Installation methods

**Homebrew (stable):** The tap is `entireio/tap`, and the cask is `entireio/tap/entire`. Use the fully qualified name, since Homebrew 6 needs third-party taps trusted first. Requires Homebrew 6.0.10+.
```
brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire
```
- Nightly: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire@nightly`

**Install script (macOS/Linux):**
```
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
```

**Windows (PowerShell 5.1+):**
```
irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex
iex "& {$(irm https://entire.io/install.ps1)} -Channel nightly"
```

**Scoop (stable only):**
```
scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
scoop install entire/entire
```
An old `cli` Scoop package needs migrating; the doc gives `cmd.exe /D /C "scoop install entire/entire && scoop uninstall entire/cli && scoop reset entire"`, run while `entire` isn't running.

**Go (manual, needs Go 1.27.1+):**
```
go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest
go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/git-remote-entire@latest
```
The second command is only needed for `entire://` URLs (e.g., `entire repo clone`).

## 2) Setting up Entire for Claude Code

1. Run `entire enable` in the repo. It creates Entire settings, installs git hooks, and prompts you to choose agent hooks.
2. Or non-interactively: `entire enable --agent claude-code`
3. Verify with `entire status`.

Useful flags: `--local` (writes `.entire/settings.local.json`), `--yes`, `--force`, `--telemetry=false`, `--skip-push-sessions`, `--checkpoint-push-remote <name>`.

**Files written:**
- `.claude/settings.json`: Claude Code JSON hook config.
- `.entire/settings.json`: project settings, including `"checkpoints": { "primary": { "type": "git-refs" } }`.
- `.entire/settings.local.json`: personal overrides, gitignored by default (only if you use `--local` or set local options).
- Git hooks: existing hooks move to `<hook>.pre-entire` and run after Entire's hook.

## 3) How checkpoints reach the remote

The doc does not mention an `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. Checkpoints are stored as per-checkpoint refs: `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`. The doc also doesn't describe a specific pre-push hook. Instead:
- `strategy_options.push_sessions` defaults to `true`, which auto-pushes checkpoint data on `git push`. `--skip-push-sessions` disables this.
- Checkpoint data goes to one elected remote, chosen in this order: `checkpoint_push_remote`, a remote captured from your push habits, `origin`, the sole remote, then the first remote in `.git/config`.
- Pushes to other remotes carry no checkpoint data, unless they point to the same GitHub repo.
- Entire never creates commits on your active branch.

## 4) Teammates after cloning

The doc gives no explicit onboarding steps. Based on the content:
- `.entire/settings.json` is typically committed, so the checkpoint backend setting comes with the clone.
- Agent hooks are detected by checking for installed hooks, so a teammate may need `entire enable --agent claude-code` to install them locally. This is an inference, not a documented step.
- Checkpoints from other machines are fetched on demand when read.
- The doc says Claude Code requires being "installed and authenticated" as a prerequisite, and it covers login (`entire login`) for accounts.

## 5) Committing `.entire` config and privacy

- Commit `.entire/settings.json` for team sharing. Keep personal overrides in `.entire/settings.local.json`, which is gitignored.
- A `settings.local.json` tracked in git is ignored entirely, and Entire says to run `git rm --cached` on it.
- A `checkpoint_remote` inherited from a committed file may be ignored if it doesn't belong to you.
- **Transcripts live in your git repo.** If the repo is public, anyone can see them.
- Entire automatically redacts detected secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) before writing, but the doc calls redaction "best-effort."
- Opt-in PII redaction, custom patterns, and scanner settings are in `docs/security-and-privacy.md`, which the doc references but doesn't include.
- Older versions created `entire/<commit>-<worktree>` shadow branches with raw working-tree blobs. Run `entire doctor` to report them and `entire doctor --force` to delete them.

**Public repo:** the auto-mode permission check blocked me from changing the visibility. I first checked the full history: there are no API keys or tokens, only the empty `.env.example`, and no Entire transcripts on GitHub yet. So it's safe to run this yourself:

```bash
gh repo edit EHL-Team-Eichel/reqflow --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences
```

Once it's public, every pushed Entire transcript is public too. Don't paste anything confidential into prompts.

**Multi-system compatibility:** I'm reading this as "works on Windows, macOS and Linux, and on laptops and phones". Tell me if you meant native desktop or mobile apps.

It's mostly there already, because it's a web app:
- **For users:** anyone with a modern browser can use it on any operating system, with nothing to install.
- **For developers:** there's no native compiling. The database is the SQLite built into Node, and the lockfile includes the Next.js, Tailwind and Vitest binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux (x64 and ARM). The code has no OS-specific parts.

What's still missing:
1. **Line endings on Windows.** There's no `.gitattributes`, so a Windows checkout gets CRLF line endings and `npm run check` fails the format check.
2. **Entire setup on Windows.** The README only gives the Homebrew command. Windows needs `irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex`.
3. **Proof.** Nothing tests it on Windows or Linux yet. A GitHub Actions run on all three systems would catch breakage on every push.
4. **Phones and tablets.** The sidebar is fixed-width and the workflow canvas is built for desktop. The Requirements page should adapt to small screens so a PM can review on a phone. A PWA manifest would also let people install it like an app.
5. **One shared URL.** For everyone to use the same app from their own devices, host it on a server with a persistent disk, such as Render, Fly or Railway. A serverless host like Vercel won't work, because the SQLite file would be wiped between requests.

**My recommendation:** stay with a single web app and don't build native apps for the hackathon. If a desktop app turns out to be required, it can be wrapped with Tauri later without a rewrite.

I can do items 1–3 now: add the `.gitattributes`, the Windows setup instructions, and a CI workflow that runs typecheck, tests and build on all three systems. Item 4 belongs to the Settings & app shell agent (WS4), and I'd add it to their task list. Want me to go ahead?
it shouldnt be a web app

# Architecture

ReqFlow is a **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron), not a web app.
Background and alternatives: [decisions/0002-electron-desktop-app.md](decisions/0002-electron-desktop-app.md).

## Stack

| Concern         | Choice                                                                                 | Why                                                                                   |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Language        | TypeScript everywhere (npm workspaces)                                                 | One shared contract for UI, engine and nodes                                          |
| App shell       | Electron 44 (pinned, Node 24 inside), electron-vite 5, electron-builder               | Same Chromium on every OS; Node in the main process runs the engine                   |
| UI              | React 19 + React Router (hash routing) + Tailwind 4                                    | Renders from `file://` in the installed app                                           |
| Workflow canvas | `@xyflow/react` (React Flow)                                                           | The standard n8n-style node editor                                                    |
| Schemas         | Zod 4                                                                                  | Runtime validation and TS types from one source; `z.toJSONSchema` drives config forms |
| LLM             | Claude API (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`) behind `LlmClient`, plus a `mock` provider            | Swappable; works offline and in tests                                                 |
| Persistence     | SQLite via built-in `node:sqlite`, in the OS app-data folder                           | Zero setup, no native module to rebuild per OS                                        |
| Tests           | Vitest (colocated `*.test.ts`) + `npm run smoke` (screenshots every screen in Electron) | Fast unit tests; a real-app check without clicking                                    |

## Repo layout

```
.
├── AGENTS.md  PRODUCT.md  README.md   ← start here
├── context/                           ← original hackathon briefing (read-only)
├── docs/                              ← ARCHITECTURE, WORKSTREAMS, decisions/ (ADRs)
├── data/
│   ├── raw/        (gitignored)       ← BMW-provided datasets
│   └── samples/                       ← small synthetic datasets for dev
├── packages/
│   ├── core/       ← CONTRACT: domain schemas, service interfaces, IPC API (ipc.ts), fixtures
│   ├── engine/     ← node contract + registry (done); graph validation + executor (WS1)
│   ├── nodes/      ← node implementations, one folder per workstream + default template
│   ├── llm/        ← LlmClient implementations: anthropic, mock (WS7)
│   └── db/         ← SQLite repositories, AuditLogger, FileStore (WS1)
└── apps/desktop/                      ← the Electron app
    ├── electron.vite.config.ts  electron-builder.yml  build/ (icons)
    └── src/
        ├── main/       ← Node: window, IPC handlers, wiring of engine/db/llm, smoke test
        ├── preload/    ← the bridge: allow-listed invoke + run-update events (keep tiny)
        └── renderer/src/
            ├── pages/  components/<area>/  router.tsx
            └── lib/api.ts             ← the only way UI code reaches the main process
```

Dependency direction (no cycles): `core ← engine ← nodes`, `core ← llm`, `core ← db`, and
`apps/desktop/src/main` → all of them. The renderer imports only `@reqflow/core` (types, constants,
fixtures). It never imports engine, db, llm or nodes.

## Processes and security

```
renderer (React, sandboxed)  ──api.x.y(…)──▶  preload (allow-list)  ──IPC──▶  main (Node)
   no Node, no fs, no network                                              engine · SQLite · LLM · files · keychain
           ◀──────────────── runs.onUpdate(run) push events ────────────────────────┘
```

- `contextIsolation`, `sandbox` and no `nodeIntegration`. Production builds get a strict CSP
  (`connect-src 'self'`): all network calls (Claude, web search) happen in main.
- The preload only forwards channels listed in `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS`. Main also checks that the sender is the app window.
- The window never navigates away. `http(s)` links open in the user's browser.
- API keys are entered in Settings, encrypted with Electron `safeStorage` (OS keychain) and never sent to
  the renderer. In dev, `apps/desktop/.env` is also read (see `.env.example`).

## IPC API (`packages/core/src/ipc.ts`)

UI code calls `api.<namespace>.<method>(…)` from `@/lib/api`. Main implements `ReqflowHandlers`
(`apps/desktop/src/main/handlers.ts`). Failures arrive as `ReqflowError` with a `code`
(`invalid_input`, `not_found`, `not_implemented`, `internal`, …). Arguments must be plain data. Main
validates every argument with the Zod schemas, because the renderer counts as untrusted input.

| Method                                                          | Purpose                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app.info()`                                                    | Version, OS, data directory                                                                                                     |
| `nodes.catalog()`                                               | `NodeCatalogEntry[]`: palette and config JSON Schema                                                                            |
| `templates.list()`                                              | Workflow templates (`BMW_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE`)                                                                                     |
| `workflows.list/get/save/remove`                                | Workflow CRUD. `save` assigns the id and bumps `version`                                                                        |
| `files.import()`                                                | Native open dialog → copies the file into the data dir → `StoredFileInfo` (`null` if cancelled)                                 |
| `runs.start/get/list/nodeOutput/resume/cancel`                  | Run lifecycle. `nodeOutput` returns that node's `PipelineData`                                                                  |
| `runs.onUpdate(listener)`                                       | Push events on every status, progress or log change (no polling)                                                                |
| `requirements.list(filter)` · `requirements.get(id)`            | Latest versions · `RequirementDetail` (findings, evidence, sources, versions)                                                   |
| `requirements.edit(id, RequirementEdit)`                        | PM edit, rationale required → new version and audit                                                                             |
| `requirements.decide(id, RequirementDecision)`                  | Approve / reject / defer / challenge / reopen. A challenge makes the AI answer (`challenge_answered`) and returns it to `in_review` |
| `audit.list(filter)`                                            | Audit events, ascending by time                                                                                                 |
| `settings.get/save` · `settings.secrets/setSecret`              | `Settings` (save logs `settings.changed` with a diff) · API-key status / store a key in the keychain                            |
| `exports.requirements({ runId, format })`                       | Native save dialog → JSON / CSV / Markdown (logs `export.created`)                                                              |

To add a method: add it to `ReqflowApi` **and** `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS` (the compiler enforces both),
then implement it in `handlers.ts`.

## Data flow: one envelope on every edge

Each node has **one input and one output**. Both are a `PipelineData`
(`sources, records, findings, themes, requirements`). A node reads the keys it `consumes` and returns
the envelope with the keys it `produces` updated. When a node has several incoming edges, the engine
combines them with `mergePipelineData` (concatenate, de-duplicate by `id`, later edge wins).

```ts
defineNode({
  type: "analysis.extract_signals",
  category: "analysis",
  consumes: ["records"],
  produces: ["findings"],

    /* ctx.llm, ctx.audit, ctx.log … */ return { status: "ok", data: { ...input, findings } };
  },

```

1. **Validate before running.** Every node type must be registered, the graph must be acyclic, edges
   must point at existing nodes, and each node's `config` must parse with its `configSchema`. If
   anything fails, the run fails before it starts, with per-node errors.
2. **Execute in topological order.** A node's input is the merge of its parents' outputs (a source
   node gets an empty envelope). Store each node's output and push `NodeRun` status, counts, logs and
   progress via `runs.onUpdate`.
3. **Failure.** A node that throws is marked `failed`, its downstream nodes `skipped`, and the run
   `failed`. Nothing is partially published.
4. **Pause / resume.** A `review.*` node returns `{status:"paused"}` → the run is

5. **Cancel.** The run's `AbortSignal` fires, and nodes must stop promptly.
6. **Audit.** The engine logs `run.*` events, nodes log what they create or change, and handlers log human actions.

- **Never trust model-cited evidence.** The model returns `recordId` and `excerpt`. Code checks that
  the excerpt is a verbatim substring of that record, and drops or flags the finding if it isn't.
- Batch the records. Use `tier: "fast"` for per-record extraction and `default` for clustering, derivation and challenges.
- AI actors in the audit trail record the exact model id returned by the client.
- The `mock` provider must return schema-valid, deterministic output so the whole pipeline runs offline.
- Prompts live next to the node that uses them (`nodes/src/<area>/<node>.prompt.ts`).

## Persistence notes (WS1)

- The database lives in the per-user app-data folder (`main/paths.ts`: macOS
  `~/Library/Application Support/ReqFlow/data`, Windows `%APPDATA%\ReqFlow\data`, Linux
  `~/.config/ReqFlow/data`). `REQFLOW_DATA_DIR` overrides it. Always build paths with `node:path`, never
  with string concatenation (Windows uses `\`).
- Only one app instance runs at a time (single-instance lock), so only one process writes SQLite.
- Requirements are versioned: one row per `(id, version)`. "Current" means the max version.
- `audit_events` is insert-only, with no update or delete code path.
- Node outputs are stored per `(runId, nodeId)` as JSON. Imported files are copied into `data/uploads/` inside the data dir.

| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| `npm run smoke`     | Builds, opens every screen, screenshots it to `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`, checks the IPC bridge, and exits non-zero on any renderer error |
| `npm run check`     | Typecheck + unit tests + format check                                                           |
| `npm run package`   | Installer for the **current** OS in `apps/desktop/release/`: `.exe` (NSIS), `.dmg` or `.AppImage` |

Gatekeeper and Windows SmartScreen show a warning on first launch. Code signing is out of scope for the
hackathon. Linux CI needs a virtual display (`xvfb-run`) for `smoke`.
